issues.legal_issue: The government may decline to confirm the highest bid in a provisional auction for a good and sufficient reason other than inadequacy of the bid, including a change or revision of policy before confirmation.
material_facts: The auction terms made acceptance of bids provisional and subject to ratification by the State Government.
The bids had not been finally ratified when the Government cancelled the auction.
The Government decided to allot the forest lots to the Forest Corporation, reverting to a policy consistent with the legislative policy for forest management and exploitation.
issues.conclusion: The Government was not obliged to accept the highest bids and could refuse them because it had changed its policy before final acceptance and decided to allot the lots to the Forest Corporation.
issues.legal_principle: Condition 10 of the auction terms made acceptance provisional and subject to ratification by the State Government; it did not restrict refusal of the highest bid to cases of inadequacy. The Uttar Pradesh Forest Corporation Act, 1974 established the Corporation and assigned it functions concerning the removal and disposal of trees and the management and development of forests entrusted to it. The Government could change its policy in the public interest, and a policy change before final acceptance was a sufficient reason to refuse a provisional bid. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.challenge_to_provisional_auction_cancell: A party challenges the government's cancellation of an auction before the provisional bids have been finally confirmed.
predicates.bids_subject_to_government_confirmation: The auction terms make acceptance of bids provisional and subject to confirmation by the government.
predicates.government_revises_policy_before_confirm: Before confirming the bids, the government changes or reverts to a policy that supports a different method of allocating or managing the subject matter.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns cancellation of an auction whose bids require government confirmation, the government may refuse the highest provisional bid if it revises its policy before confirmation.

issues.legal_issue: Cancelling provisional forest auctions and allotting the forest lots to a government-owned corporation in accordance with forest-preservation policy was not arbitrary or invalid for failure to state reasons.
material_facts: The legislative policy favored the Forest Corporation undertaking forest work, and the Government had previously decided to allot forest lots to it.

The highest bids were substantially above the estimated price, and forest officials considered them suspicious in light of the risk of illicit felling; an incident also disrupted the last day of the auction.
The Government cancelled the auctions and allotted the lots to the Corporation, and its communication stated that the auctions were cancelled because the lots would be worked through the Corporation.

The Corporation was government-owned and dedicated to forest preservation, development, and exploitation of forest produce; the Government's interests therefore extended beyond obtaining the highest immediate revenue.
issues.conclusion: The Government's decision had a good and sufficient reason, conformed to legislative policy, and was not arbitrary merely because the Corporation might pay less than the auction bids; the decision was not invalid for failure to state reasons.
issues.legal_principle: The Government's discretion under the auction terms was not confined to rejecting inadequate bids. It could act on a good and sufficient reason, including implementing the legislative policy embodied in the Uttar Pradesh Forest Corporation Act, 1974. The State's interests included preservation and development of forests as well as revenue, and the communicated decision identified allotment to the Corporation as the reason for cancellation. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.challenge_to_government_allotment_after_: A party challenges the government's cancellation of auction results and subsequent allotment of the subject matter to a public entity.
predicates.government_policy_favors_public_forest_m: The government has a policy, consistent with the legislature's direction, favoring management and exploitation of forest resources through a public corporation.
predicates.communicated_reason_identifies_policy_ba: The government communicates that it cancelled the auction because it decided to have the forest lots worked through the public corporation.
predicates.state_interest_includes_resource_preserv: The government has an interest in preserving and developing forest resources in addition to obtaining revenue.

issues.definition: When a challenged cancellation and allotment implements a forest-management policy, the government communicates that policy-based reason, and its interests include preservation as well as revenue, the decision is not arbitrary or invalid for lack of reasons.
